lightingIsotropy.method: 36-bin luminance-gradient orientation census over non-water pixels; this is a mechanical isotropy measure, not visual acceptance.

surfaceFractions.method: Water is the traced alpha-mask footprint; coherent level bench tops and approach shelves count as buildable, while exposed bench faces, arch faces, talus, scree fans, and broken transition slopes count as steep.

crown.method: Full-frame grid census of every discernible outer-foliage conifer crown, including saplings and clipped edge crowns; source widths were scaled by 2560/1254 and converted at 0.048 m per final pixel.

visualReview.status: quarantine candidate; hard-constraint failure observed; pending director and owner inspection
claims: Three pale basalt benches, their exposed column faces, and talus feet dominate the cell while the outer ground grades into the painted neighbour families.
The round middle-bench tarn has a complete shingle rim with no vegetation touching its masked water surface.
The eastern upper bench provides a natural arch and adjacent level rock shelf; the northern bench provides an unbuilt rock face and approach ground.
hardConstraintFindings: The visible groove reaches the west edge near source y=260 and the east edge near source y=390, not the required approximately y=602 and y=564 seam handoffs.
The western fall visibly begins at the same cut line at the bench lip, so the image does not establish the required dry rune slot.
openRisks: The carved slot appears shallower and more kerbed than the specified two-metre-deep bedrock excavation in parts of the image.
Mechanical isotropy does not prove the strict no-key-light visual rule; exposed column faces still need human inspection for orientation-dependent value.
